references: Native iOS typography, spacing, and control hierarchy

contract.purpose: Help a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, capture what changes it, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.canonicalPurpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.audience: A person moving between Mac, iPhone, and Apple Watch who wants a deliberate day rather than another task list.
contract.job: Build or confirm today's schedule, focus the current block, capture interruptions without friction, and review planned versus lived time.
contract.thesis: The Drawn Day pairs calm native controls with authored doodles so planning feels human while schedule state stays precise.
contract.system: Neutral paper and charcoal surfaces, native SF typography, a chronological day rail, one high-contrast action, warm interruption-origin colors, and one purposeful doodle per primary surface.
contract.signature: The same drawn-day line moves from the Today schedule into Focus context and returns as the planned-versus-lived trace in History.
contract.risk: Doodle-first personality can crowd an operating surface; each screen limits art to one purposeful scene that yields to controls and collapses as density rises.

projectCheck.command: swift test; release anchor-mcp --diagnose; DebugLocal xcodebuild for macOS, iOS Simulator, and watchOS Simulator; stable-Xcode iOS UI journeys; seven isolated macOS UI journeys; ios-landings pnpm check and responsive review
projectCheck.note: All 153 package tests, the 8/8 distraction and 4/4 goal diagnostic, and DebugLocal macOS, iOS, and watchOS builds pass. On a fresh iOS 26.5 simulator, all four UI journeys reached their passing assertions. Seven isolated native Mac journeys now pass together, covering Focus persistence, Today scheduling and review, usual-week routines, habits, History and exports, Mini Timer, onboarding, and Settings. Fresh Today, Focus, Habits, History, and Watch renders were inspected directly; ios-landings passes all eight product builds and required routes, plus Anchor review at 390, 768, and 1440 pixels.

ownerFeedback.note: Round 0 rejected: the Day Overlay and Focus Viewfinder felt too simple and basic; Departure Lines had welcome authorship but its literal depot-board execution did not earn selection. Round 1 was rejected as too funky. The owner pinned the world to simple, premium, and doodle-first, selected Doodle Scene as the structural base, rejected the first repeated selector drawings, and asked for neutral chrome so authored colour could pop. The owner approved the implemented direction on 2026-08-25 and requested one final button refinement. Primary, quiet, and transport controls now share shallow physical depth and settle-on-press feedback. Dark is now the shared product default, with one iCloud-backed System, Light, or Dark choice for every Anchor device. The owner then asked for signup inside onboarding, a stronger Settings account experience, a real Google mark, and verified top-toolbar behavior; the shared Hub panel and responsive six-stage onboarding now carry that direction. The final account composition is viewport-centered, uses compact secondary actions, and leaves Mac window chrome entirely to the native title bar.
